extra.message: Path traversal in user_pic(): filename from request.GET.get('p') is concatenated with base_path and passed to open() without validation. An attacker can supply paths like '../../etc/passwd' to read arbitrary files on the server.

Remote Code Execution in code_execution(): exec() is invoked on base64-decoded user input (request.POST.get('first_name', '')). An attacker can submit arbitrary Python code which will be executed on the server, leading to full compromise.

Arbitrary function invocation in unvalidated_forward(): the 'fwd' query parameter is used to look up a function in globals() and invoke it with the request. An attacker can call any function defined in the module (e.g., boom, admin, dor_user_profile, code_execution) to trigger unintended behavior, including RCE via exec-based endpoints.

Open redirect in unvalidated_redirect(): the 'url' query parameter is passed directly to Django's redirect() with no validation. An attacker can craft a link that redirects users to a malicious external site (phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: Missing function-level access control in missing_access_control(): any unauthenticated user can access the admin page simply by appending '?action=admin' to the URL. There is no authentication or authorization check before rendering the admin template.

Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in dor_user_profile(): the userid is taken directly from the URL and used to look up and display (and via POST, modify) any user record in the in-memory users dict, including the admin user (id=2). There is no authentication or ownership check.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: CSRF protection is disabled with @csrf_exempt on csrf_image(). State-changing operations (and even rendering with cookie context) become vulnerable to cross-site request forgery attacks from attacker-controlled sites.

DEBUG = True is hardcoded in settings.py. Running with DEBUG enabled in production exposes detailed stack traces, settings, environment variables, and SQL queries to any user triggering an error (e.g., via the /misconfiguration/boom view).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY in settings.py. A leaked SECRET_KEY allows attackers to forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, password reset tokens, and any other value signed by Django's signing framework.

django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware is commented out of MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES, disabling CSRF protection globally for the entire application. Combined with the @csrf_exempt csrf_image view, this exposes the app to CSRF attacks.

show_toolbar() allows the Django Debug Toolbar to be enabled by any unauthenticated user simply by supplying a 'debug' GET/POST parameter or cookie. The toolbar exposes SQL queries, settings, request data, and other sensitive internals to remote attackers.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
